chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayyna, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
'Allah created the Will by itself, then created the things through the Will.'

key_terms.الْأَشْيَاءَ: the things — all created entities besides the Will itself
key_terms.الْمَشِيئَةَ: Divine Will (al-Mashiyya) — the primordial creative principle through which all things come into existence; it is itself created but serves as the instrument for all subsequent creation
key_terms.بِنَفْسِهَا: by itself — indicating the Will was created without any prior instrument or intermediary, unlike all other created things

ai.seo_question: How did Allah create the Divine Will and all other things according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the ontological primacy of the Divine Will (al-Mashiyya) in the act of creation. Unlike all other created things which come into being through the mediation of the Will, the Will itself was created directly by Allah without any prior instrument — it is self-grounded in God's creative act. This hadith belongs to the theological discussions in Kitab al-Tawhid of al-Kafi, addressing questions about the relationship between God's attributes and His creative activity, distinguishing the Mashiyya as a special intermediary between the uncaused divine essence and all contingent beings.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Axina, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created the Desire by itself, then Created the things with the Desire’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “
Allah created His Will by Will itself. Then, He created all things by His Will.”
